Laboratory findings: serum calcium 1.95 mmol/L (normal: 2.05-2.55), serum phosphorus 3.3 mmol/L (normal: 0.74-1.52), serum intact parathyroid hormone 142 ng/L (normal: 10-65), serum creatinine 787 μmol/L (normal: 53-106).

data.description: Ectopic, lobulated periarticular or soft‑tissue calcium‑phosphate deposits that occur in patients with chronic kidney disease, driven by hyperphosphatemia and secondary/tertiary hyperparathyroidism.
symptoms_in_common: Long‑standing end‑stage renal disease on dialysis
Slowly enlarging, firm, immobile subcutaneous mass
symptoms_not_in_common: Lumbar location (classically periarticular around hips/shoulders/elbows, though ectopic sites can occur)

data.diagnosis: Metastatic soft‑tissue calcification due to secondary hyperparathyroidism in CKD
data.description: Widespread calcium‑phosphate deposition in normal tissues (skin, subcutaneous tissue, blood vessels, periarticular regions) due to elevated calcium–phosphate product in chronic kidney disease with secondary hyperparathyroidism.
symptoms_in_common: Potential radiographic soft‑tissue calcifications near joints
symptoms_not_in_common: Solitary large mass (metastatic calcification is often multifocal/diffuse rather than a single discrete tumor‑like mass)
Completely asymptomatic presentation (some cases cause stiffness or discomfort)

data.description: Medial calcification and thrombosis of small arterioles in patients with advanced kidney disease, typically presenting with painful, rapidly progressive skin ischemia leading to necrotic ulcers.
symptoms_in_common: Disordered mineral metabolism with elevated PTH
symptoms_not_in_common: Asymptomatic mass (calciphylaxis lesions are usually very painful)
No skin discoloration, livedo, or ulceration
Slow growth over 6 months (calciphylaxis typically progresses rapidly)
Firm immobile subcutaneous nodule rather than indurated plaques/eschar

data.description: Deposition of monosodium urate crystals forming tophi in soft tissues and around joints, usually after long‑standing hyperuricemia; masses can be firm and may calcify.
symptoms_not_in_common: Absence of a history of gout flares
Location in lumbar subcutaneous tissue rather than typical periarticular sites (ears, olecranon, fingers, toes, Achilles)
Marked hyperphosphatemia and elevated PTH (not features of gout)
Dialysis‑related mineral bone disorder better explains findings

data.diagnosis: Extraskeletal osteosarcoma or calcified soft‑tissue sarcoma
data.description: A rare malignant soft‑tissue tumor that produces osteoid and can present as a firm, enlarging, calcified mass in soft tissues, usually in older adults.
symptoms_in_common: Possible calcifications within soft tissue on imaging
symptoms_not_in_common: Asymptomatic over 6 months (sarcomas often become painful or cause functional symptoms)
Strong association with severe hyperphosphatemia and elevated PTH is lacking
Renal failure and mineral imbalance better explain calcific mass without other malignant features

A 52-year-old woman presented with complaints of anal pain, constipation, and tenesmus for 3 months before being referred to the hospital. There were no relevant prior illnesses. Rectal digital examination revealed a 6-cm smooth elastic mass on the rectal posterior left side 2 cm from the anal verge. Colonoscopy showed a rectal submucosal bulging. Computed tomography scan and magnetic resonance imaging confirmed the presence of a single 6-cm well-delimited mass, compressing and infiltrating the wall of the medium to low rectum.

data.description: Mesenchymal tumor arising from interstitial cells of Cajal; often presents as a well-circumscribed submucosal mass in the rectum. Can cause pain, obstructive symptoms, and tenesmus; may infiltrate the rectal wall.
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported overt rectal bleeding (often present in GIST)
No mention of systemic symptoms or anemia
No reported ulceration on endoscopy

data.description: Tumors derived from smooth muscle of the rectal wall; can be benign (leiomyoma) or malignant (leiomyosarcoma). Typically form a submucosal, palpable mass and may cause pain and obstructive symptoms.
symptoms_in_common: Palpable smooth elastic submucosal mass near the anal verge
Imaging shows a single, well-defined mass with mural involvement
symptoms_not_in_common: No reported ulceration or bleeding (more typical for leiomyosarcoma)
No rapid systemic decline or metastasis signs noted

data.description: Benign peripheral nerve sheath tumor that can arise in the rectum, usually appearing as a well-circumscribed submucosal lesion and causing symptoms by mass effect.
symptoms_in_common: Anal pain and tenesmus from mass effect
Palpable smooth mass on digital rectal exam
symptoms_not_in_common: Imaging suggests wall infiltration (schwannomas are typically noninfiltrative/encapsulated)
Constipation is less characteristic than for other rectal masses
No mention of mucosal ulceration which can sometimes occur

data.description: Neuroendocrine neoplasm commonly arising in the distal rectum; typically submucosal. Small lesions are common, but larger tumors can present with local invasion and obstructive symptoms.
symptoms_in_common: Tenesmus and constipation from local mass effect
symptoms_not_in_common: Large size (6 cm) is uncommon for typical rectal NETs
No carcinoid syndrome features (flushing, diarrhea, wheezing)
Described as well-delimited rather than the more typical small, firm nodule

data.diagnosis: Deep infiltrating endometriosis involving the rectal wall
data.description: Ectopic endometrial tissue infiltrating the rectovaginal septum/rectum, forming nodular masses that can narrow the lumen and cause pain and altered bowel habits.
symptoms_in_common: Low rectal mass effect with constipation and tenesmus
symptoms_not_in_common: Age (52 years) and lack of cyclic pain or menstrual correlation
Colonoscopy showing a smooth submucosal bulge without mucosal changes is compatible but less typical
No gynecologic symptoms documented (dyspareunia, dysmenorrhea)

data.description: Lymphoid malignancy involving the colon/rectum that can present as a submucosal or polypoid mass with local infiltration and obstructive symptoms.
symptoms_in_common: Single large rectal mass with mural infiltration
symptoms_not_in_common: Well-delimited appearance is less typical (lymphoma often appears bulky and infiltrative)
No B symptoms (fever, night sweats, weight loss)
No lymphadenopathy reported

http_response.description:
Two-year-four-month-old female with IUGR at birth after Cesarean delivery at 39 weeks for placental insufficiency; birth weight 1850 g, length 44.5 cm, and head circumference 31 cm, all at the 3rd percentile. At 3 months, suspected hearing loss was evaluated with ABR showing bilateral severe sensorineural hearing loss, and hearing aids were placed at 4 months. During infancy, she had persistent growth delay with weight and height below the 3rd percentile, while psychomotor development was normal (sitting at 8 months, walking at 14 months, talking at 13 months). CNS MRI was normal. Genetic testing identified a de novo heterozygous PIK3R1 variant c.1956dupT (p.Lys653*) in exon 15.

data.description: A benign primary cardiac tumor of childhood composed of fibroblasts and dense collagen; most often a solitary intramural mass in the left ventricle or septum. On MRI it is typically T1 isointense, T2 hypointense with strong late gadolinium enhancement; grossly firm and white; histology shows bland spindle cells in dense collagen with slit-like vessels.
symptoms_in_common: Solitary ventricular mass on echocardiography and cardiac MRI
Histology with dense collagen and sparse vessels consistent with fibroma
Strong late gadolinium enhancement on MRI
symptoms_not_in_common: Intrauterine growth restriction
Postnatal poor growth
Severe bilateral sensorineural hearing loss
De novo PIK3R1 truncating variant

data.diagnosis: Cardiac rhabdomyoma (often associated with tuberous sclerosis complex)
data.description: The most common pediatric cardiac tumor, composed of hamartomatous cardiac myocytes. Frequently multiple, intraventricular, and may regress spontaneously. Strongly associated with tuberous sclerosis complex.
symptoms_in_common: Intraventricular cardiac mass detected in infancy/early childhood
symptoms_not_in_common: Mass is solitary and appears fibrous/firm rather than myocyte-rich
Strong late gadolinium enhancement (rhabdomyomas typically do not show intense LGE)
Histology lacks spider cells typical of rhabdomyoma
No features of tuberous sclerosis complex reported (e.g., cortical tubers, skin lesions)
Sensorineural hearing loss and IUGR are not characteristic

data.description: A benign neoplasm of myxoid stroma, most commonly arising in the left atrium as a pedunculated, mobile mass; rare in young children, can be sporadic or part of Carney complex.
symptoms_not_in_common: Location appears intramural in the ventricle rather than a pedunculated atrial mass
Gross specimen is firm/whitish rather than gelatinous myxoid
Histology does not show myxoid stroma with myxoma cells and vascular channels typical of myxoma
Age is younger than typical sporadic cases
IUGR and SNHL are not typical features

data.description: A blood clot forming within a cardiac chamber, usually in areas of akinesis or dilatation, or in the setting of indwelling lines, hypercoagulability, or myocarditis; typically non-enhancing on MRI.
symptoms_not_in_common: Mass shows strong late gadolinium enhancement (thrombi typically show no or only peripheral enhancement)
Gross specimen is solid tumor, not friable clot
Histology shows collagenous tumor rather than organized thrombus
No reported predisposing cardiac dysfunction or catheters
IUGR and SNHL are unrelated

data.diagnosis: SHORT syndrome due to PIK3R1 pathogenic variant
data.description: A multisystem developmental disorder caused by heterozygous loss-of-function variants in PIK3R1. Hallmarks include intrauterine growth restriction, postnatal growth failure, characteristic facial features, lipoatrophy, insulin resistance/diabetes in later childhood, and variably sensorineural hearing loss.
symptoms_in_common: De novo heterozygous PIK3R1 truncating variant (p.Lys653*)
symptoms_not_in_common: Cardiac fibroma/intraventricular tumor not typically part of SHORT syndrome
No description of characteristic facial features or lipoatrophy
No insulin resistance/diabetes reported (may emerge later)
